title: Working with so many black musicians: Leeman's view
summary: Leeman says black musicians liked his playing first, quoting Dan Morgenstern that Condon ignored race as if it did not exist.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: There's been an urgent prodding in the base of my mind or in the back of my mind, I should say, to get this off my chest. The black and white issue, or -- if you wish, the problems involved in my career racially.
So many have asked how come I worked with so many great black musicians and groups, and my answer -- they liked my playing first, and then me personally, I suppose. As I did them.

God has been kind to me, to bestow me with a sense and feeling of love for all people -- and enough talent for them to accept me as a participating fellow musician. It brings to mind an observation -- and I believe that it was writer /critic Dan Morganstern in his evaluation of Eddie Condon. He said Eddie Condon ignored the racial issue as if it didn't exist. And them is my sentiments.
Of course you realize it's there, and it does exist to too many people.
